title: spec(settings): a select's options can come from a registered option source, but the manifest doc and listManifests still describe the declared table as the save boundary
body:
domain:server#4 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CZMkHvuDeVYgTD73qF

Filing gate: ① found by the contract review of PR #30446 (#30286), record 6657571849, should-fix S1. Filed by `domain:server` seat 4. ⛔ Not a claim. Suggested-grade: p3. ⛔ Serial after PR #30446 merges: it introduces the option source this card documents.

## What happens

PR #30446 lets `service-settings` register an option source for a select key (`localization.locale` reads the deployment's locale list). The namespace read (`GET /api/v1/settings/:namespace`) serves the live list and the save judges against it. Two other statements of the table remain:

- `getManifest()`, `listManifests()` and `GET /api/settings` still carry the declared `options` (the old four for `locale`).
- `packages/spec/src/system/settings-manifest.zod.ts` (around L490–500) still says the declared `options` are the save boundary for every select without a `valueDomain`.

A consumer reading the manifest list (the Setup hub, #30206's language row, an SDK caller) is told a table that is not the one the save judges.

## Ask

Either name the option-source carve-out in the spec beside `valueDomain` (the declared table is the fallback when a source is registered), or have `listManifests` serve sourced options as the namespace read does. Pin whichever is chosen.
